scores.claim_text: 85% of 2023 net sales from proprietary products/solutions, underpinned by patents, trademarks, trade secrets and proprietary knowledge.
scores.M_check: uspto_odp.query_assignee (assignee 'Loar' -> 0 granted; assignee 'Schroth' -> 25 applications / 12 granted patents, e.g. occupant-restraint / airbag CPC B60R 21)
scores.M_value: Loar parent: 0 granted patents. SCHROTH (acquired brand): n_total_applications=25, n_granted=12, all in safety-restraint technology consistent with the product line.
scores.interpretation: Parent-name patent search is empty, but the proprietary-IP moat here is correctly trade-secret + qualification-based (the prospectus itself stresses certification barriers, not patent counts), and the named acquired brand SCHROTH carries a real granted-patent portfolio (12) directly in its product category. Brand-level corroboration confirms genuine proprietary technology. Not the Nikola pattern (no large patent claim was even made). PASS.

scores.claim_text: Defense/military aviation ~19% of 2023 net sales ($59.2M); supplier to A&D OEMs and Tier 1/2; revenue follows the U.S. DoD budget.
scores.M_value: signal=RECURRING_FEDERAL; 5 UEIs resolved; n_contracts=556; contracts_amount_M=$21.06M; 51 DoD contracts (+1 HHS); top awards to SCHROTH SAFETY PRODUCTS LLC and SMR ACQUISITION LLC (Army W56HZV, DLA SPE/SPRDL, Navy N6133) of $0.75M-$2.16M each.
scores.interpretation: Independent federal registry corroborates real, recurring DoD presence across the operating brands, exactly matching the disclosed defense exposure. The parent 'Loar Group Inc.' UEI shows $0 directly (consistent with the cohort note that most A&D content is subcontracted/indirect and flows through the operating subsidiaries), while the named brands hold the actual DoD obligations. Strong PASS.

scores.claim_text: 16 acquisitions since 2012, including SCHROTH (2022), DAC (2023), CAV (2023), with recorded goodwill of $104.0M / $17.5M / $12.1M.
scores.M_value: EDGAR FTS total_hits=25 for SCHROTH (incl. TransDigm Group 10-Q/8-K references to the SCHROTH product line under prior ownership), confirming SCHROTH is a real, externally-recognized A&D brand. USPTO confirms SCHROTH SAFETY PRODUCTS LLC as a real assignee with 12 granted patents.
scores.interpretation: The acquired brands are real, registry-recorded operating entities (SCHROTH has USPTO patents and an FPDS/USAspending UEI with DoD awards; CAV Aerospace and Despatch Industries also resolve to UEIs). Acquisition narrative independently corroborated. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Top two aircraft platforms are the Airbus A320 family and the Boeing 737 family; serves >250 platforms across >84,000 installed aircraft; no platform >6% of sales.
scores.M_value: GE Aerospace filings: 0 hits for 'Loar'. RTX/Pratt & Whitney filings: 0 hits for 'Loar'.
scores.interpretation: No registry covers platform-level component qualification, and large airframe/engine OEMs do not separately disclose a Tier 2/3 niche-component supplier by name (Heuristic 5: a sub-material B2B subcontract relationship is simply not disclosed by the buyer). Zero OEM mentions is the EXPECTED result for an indirect/subcontracted component maker and is not a contradiction. The diversification claim (no platform >6%) is internally consistent and not independently testable. UNVERIFIABLE (honestly), not SEVERE.

scores.claim_text: $317M 2023 net sales at 36% Adj. EBITDA margin; real manufacturing operations (PP&E $122M gross, inventories $78M); $103.8M foreign sales.
scores.M_value: signal=NO_OSHA_FOOTPRINT; 0 establishments under the parent name 'Loar'.
scores.interpretation: OSHA 300A absence under the PARENT brand is non-informative here (Heuristic 6): Loar operates through ~15 separately-named brand subsidiaries (SCHROTH, CAV Aerospace, Despatch, SMR, etc.), so a parent-name OSHA search would not surface its plants even though they exist. The audited financials (PP&E, inventories, foreign sales, end-market revenue table) are self-consistent with a real operating manufacturer, but no single federal registry confirms the consolidated scale under the parent name. UNVERIFIABLE rather than underdelivery.

scores.claim_text: $539.2M term loans at 12.7% WAIR, substantially all held by Blackstone Credit, with $525.4M maturing in 2026; IPO proceeds used to repay debt.
scores.M_check: Prospectus internal financial-statement disclosure (Note 8 Long-Term Debt; Note 18 Related-Party); going-concern screen of own filings
scores.M_value: No going-concern / substantial-doubt language in the 424B4. Debt fully disclosed: $539.2M outstanding, 12.7% WAIR, 2026 maturity wall, Blackstone Credit as sole lender; IPO ($28.00 x 11.0M primary = ~$308M gross) earmarked to de-lever.
scores.interpretation: High leverage and a 2026 maturity wall are real risks, but they are FULLY and honestly disclosed in the prospectus, with the IPO explicitly structured to pay down debt. This is candid disclosure of a known risk rather than concealment or underdelivery. Under the honesty-alpha framework, transparent bad-news disclosure scores PASS (the framework excludes liars, not levered companies). PASS.
